subject: Architecture
title: The Golden Gate Bridge: Art in Steel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Golden Gate Bridge: Art in Steel.

hook.text: Engineers said a bridge across San Francisco Bay was impossible. Joseph Strauss proved them wrong.

buildup.text: At 4,200 feet, the Golden Gate was the world's longest suspension span when it opened in 1937.

discovery.text: The signature 'International Orange' paint wasn't planned — it was the primer color, and everyone loved it.

twist.text: A safety net under the deck saved 19 workers during construction. They called themselves the 'Halfway to Hell Club.'

climax.text: The bridge uses 80,000 miles of wire in its cables — enough to circle the Earth three times.

punchline.text: Impossible. Until someone built it in orange.

quiz.question: Why is the Golden Gate Bridge painted 'International Orange'?
options: It was the primer color that everyone loved and kept
Orange is most visible in San Francisco fog
The Navy required a bright color for ship visibility
